results.title: Enlightening, Beautiful & Humbling
results.text: This is one of the Hindu's most holy temple complexes. They charge visitors into the complex. It's about 10 quid which I thought expensive. Each day there are cremations going on at the side of the river. Please be aware this is all in full public view. They bless the bodies near the water's edge and they are carried along the river and put on a pyre. The family then light the pyre, ashes to ashes. It's extremely humbling and sometimes hard viewing seeing families in such emotional turmoil all out in public. There are a lot of people begging and lots of homeless people around the temple. All trying to make a tourist dollar. The complex itself like most of Kathmandu has been badly damaged by the quake. There are also lots of "holy men" around, they are all fully body painted, if you take their photo they will demand money from you, be warned. Really worth a visit though as a westerner, opened my eyes.

results.title: Temple with monkeys
results.text: Famous about this temple monkeys are everywhere and cremations happen by the river. Monkeys are mostly harmless and not wild. Watching the cremations is very strange experience you can watch very close and see the body parts either and you can smell burning flesh. So it is interesting but definitely not easy, be consider before you visit. Photographers can catch very nice captures. Not appropriate for children.

results.title: Holy place, a must visit for devotees
results.text: I went there in the month of February, a few days before Mahashivratri. The temple was nearly empty with enough time to take darshan. We could spend plenty of time in its vicinity, see the sadhus sitting in the temple premises and soak in the spiritual atmostphere.

results.title: Holy site for Hindus, must-see open air cremation site for the rest of us
results.text:
This is a vast compound of buildings which hosts one of the holiest sites for Hindus. The $10 admission fee does not give you access to the temple itself, which is unfortunately off limits for non-Hindus.
But you are here to witness the unbelievable (for westerns) open air cremation rituals, which happen around the clock. Yes, of course it's off-putting for the faint of heart, especially when the wind blows ashes everywhere.
Lots of monkeys (plus dogs, cows, sheep) but also holy men/beggars who are happy to pose for you if you spare a dollar.

results.title: Hindus' most important temple in Nepal
results.text: The title of my review is true, but I should add that when you are a foreigner (white skinned), they charge an entry fee which is quite high. While one of my friends is a beef-eating Afro-American, and due to his skin color he could enter the holy Golden Temple, which is accessible only for Hindus, me, who is a vegetarian and practice Yoga, was barred... I don't like the discriminatory rule, at least it should not be based on skin color but some other criteria... But anyway, I felt elevated and overwhelmed by the air of this ancient temple complex, which reminded me somehow of Varanasi in India...

results.title: Kathmandu's most famous heritage
results.text:
Many call Kathmandu, the city of the Pashupatinath and therefore, one of the holiest cities in the world. This amazing heritage is a Hindu marvel. Hundreds of temples of all major gods grace the main temple of Lord Shiva, the most revered and storied God in Hinduism. The temple is a architectural marvel as well with its famous doors and pagoda-styled roofs.
The temple area is huge with multiple hidden temples and places. One really needs to have enough time to explore the entire area. The river that flows beside the temple (Bagmati) is cleaner than it was and steps have been taken to stop pollution. The only downside to this immense heritage is the fact that entry to the main temple premise (although there is still much much to see around despite this) is allowed only to the Hindus. As all global religions market themselves and invite conversions, Hinduism shies away from such exposure and therefore, entry is restricted. I really don't know how to comment on this but the temple is still visible mostly from outside its walls.
The evening aarati (prayers with music and oil-lights) in the temple is a delight as well. Something definitely not to miss.
